summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming on the "add logging" brief, explicitly classified it as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a multi-question design dialogue, wrote docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-browser-logging-design.md, presented it for review with no source code touched, and only moved to writing-plans after I said "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is supported by direct evidence from the session log, the workdir filesystem, and the screen. The router escalated the ambiguous \"add logging\" brief to the architectural path, produced a spec document, gated on human approval, and only then proceeded to writing-plans. Incidental oddities (gitignored/uncommitted spec, ungated-review ledger note) are recorded as observations, not failures.

observations.description: The agent added a .gitignore containing `docs/hyperpowers` and `docs/superpowers` and explicitly stated the spec was "not committed" and deliberately kept out of commits. The spec therefore lives only as an untracked working-tree file — if a workflow expects a committed spec artifact, this defeats it.
HOWTO says dialog-bypass state is seeded in the isolated $HOME, but on launch I still had to answer four startup dialogs (theme picker, security notes, folder-trust, bypass-permissions warning).

The agent mentioned an "ungated ledger (20260917T024934Z-40737-25823)" flagging that the spec shipped without independent review (Codex preflight reported version `0.0.0-stub`). Confusing to a human partner — it implies a review gate silently degraded.
Mid-design the agent asked "Does that look right so far?" which reads like an approval gate but was only a checkpoint; a tester could easily mistake it for the real spec-review gate.

The brainstorming dialogue was long: seven question screens (some multi-tab with Submit tabs) plus several minutes of generated prose per step ("Churned for 4m 32s", "Sautéed for 3m 58s"). Cute spinner verbs aside, a lot of scrolled-off text is hard to review before answering.
Spec doc header says "Status: Approved design" even though it was written before the human had approved it; status should start as 'proposed'.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: `grep -o 'hyperpowers:[a-z-]*' <session>.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` returned "36 hyperpowers:brainstorming"; skill loaded at the start, before any file edits (only file_path writes in log are the spec and codex-review cache files).

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec doc to docs/.../specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in log: "**Classification: architectural.** \"Logging\" is a new subsystem — there's no logging module, no log destination, no levels, no redaction, nothing to extend." Spec file exists: /coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-browser-logging-design.md, beginning "# Browser Logging Subsystem — Design ... Status: Approved design, pending implementation plan".

criteria.criterion: Spec surfaced for review and approval requested before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-browser-logging-design.md — not committed. ... No source files touched; no code written." and "Please review the spec and let me know if you want changes before I move on to writing the implementation plan." `git status --short` in the workdir showed only `?? .gitignore` — no source edits.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: No bounded self-classification appeared in assistant turns; the only assistant classification line was "Classification: architectural", and a spec file was in fact written (see path above). Grep over assistant text for bounded/spike returned only skill-document (user-role) matches.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: Same grep: no assistant turn proposes a spike or probe; the flow went classification → design questions → spec doc → approval → "Spec approved. Per the architectural path, the next and only step is the writing-plans skill." (screen).
